payload.unsafe_pattern: An async event handler (button onClick, IntersectionObserver callback, etc.) that is refactored from direct DOM mutation into a `state()` value written from an `effect()`, but the post-await `.set(...)` calls inside the async callback are not guarded by the component's `createFactoryScope().signal.aborted` check before writing. Two of five near-identical refactors merged in this window ( #15434 account-menu, #15475 configuration-view) omitted the guard that the other three (#15419 ui-primitives, #15463 table-region, #15483 data-view) added for the same busy/status-state extraction.
payload.consequence: If the component unmounts (user navigates away) while the awaited async work (clipboard copy, OAuth switch/logout fetch, diagnostics collection) is still pending, the callback resumes after await and calls `.set()` on reactive state whose effect still writes to now-detached DOM nodes. This is at minimum a wasted write to disposed state and, if the effect's cleanup already ran, a null/stale-reference write; the exact bug class the sibling PRs' tests (`ignores a continuation load that resolves after ... removed`, `stops writing ... once its boundary is detached`) were added specifically to catch and prevent.
payload.mechanical_correction: After every `await` inside an async handler that subsequently calls `state.set(...)`, check `if (scope.signal.aborted) return;` (or the component's equivalent abort signal) before performing the write, mirroring the guard already present in #15419, #15463, and #15483.

evidence.title: Extract createCopyControl run state into reactive state and effect
evidence.detail: Added `if (scope.signal.aborted) return;` immediately after `await copyTextToClipboard(...)` and before the subsequent `busy.set(false)`/`copyState.set(...)` writes.

evidence.title: Extract table-region continuation-load busy state into reactive state and effect
evidence.detail: Added `if (continuationScope.signal.aborted) return;` after the awaited `options.continuation.load(...)` call in both the success and catch paths, and guarded the `finally` block's `continuationBusy.set(false)` with the same check. Added two regression tests: one asserting the button stays disabled and no error dataset is set once removed, another asserting a stale resolution after removal does not reinsert rows.

evidence.title: Extract mobile card-list continuation busy state into reactive state and effect
evidence.detail: Wrapped the continuation-load state in `state()`/`effect()` bound to `boundaryScope.signal`; regression test 'stops writing the mobile card continuation load state once its boundary is detached' explicitly asserts a post-removal async resolution does not mutate `boundary.dataset.loadState`.

evidence.title: Extract account-menu switch/logout busy state into reactive state and effect
evidence.detail: Same busy-state extraction pattern (`switchBusy`/`logoutBusy` state + single effect writing `switchButton.disabled`/`logoutButton.disabled`) applied to two awaited fetch-based handlers (`switchAccount`, `logout`), but neither handler checks any abort/detached signal before its post-await `busy.set(false)` write; no regression test for a post-unmount resolution was added, unlike the sibling PRs.

evidence.title: Extract configuration-view diagnostics busy state into reactive state and effect
evidence.detail: Same extraction pattern applied to the awaited `collectFullDiagnostics()` + `copyTextToClipboard(...)` handler; `diagnosticsBusy.set(false)`/`diagnosticsStatusText.set(...)` in the try/catch/finally body have no abort-signal guard despite the component already owning a `createFactoryScope()` (`scope`) used for its other effect, and despite the nearly identical `createCopyControl` (#15419, merged in the same window) adding the guard for the same copy-to-clipboard flow.

syntactic_constructs: async () => { ... await ...; ...State.set(...); } inside an onClick/observer callback
createFactoryScope() + state() + effect({ signal: scope.signal }) component shape (reactive.js, factory-elements.js)
missing `if (scope.signal.aborted) return;` directly after an awaited call and before a subsequent `.set()`
payload.likely_false_positives: An async handler that calls `.set()` after `await` but whose component is never removed from the DOM during that async work (e.g. a top-level page-scoped singleton that outlives all navigation) does not need the guard; the rule should only fire when the enclosing scope is created via `createFactoryScope()`/bound to a removable node, i.e. an abort signal is already available in scope but unused after an await preceding a `.set()` call.
payload.existing_plugin_coverage: No published ESLint rule covers this: it depends on recognizing this repo's specific `reactive.js` state/effect/createFactoryScope convention and its abort-signal idiom, not a generic async/await or React-hooks pattern that an existing plugin (eslint-plugin-react-hooks, eslint-plugin-promise, etc.) targets.

payload.unsafe_pattern: A JavaScript/TypeScript test asserts (via assert.match/toMatch/toContain with a regex or exact string) a specific hex color or color-mix() literal value copied out of a themed/visual source file (e.g. docs/components/*.astro dark-mode CSS custom properties), instead of asserting only the structural property (selector exists, variable name defined, contrast ratio computed) that the test is actually meant to guard.
payload.consequence: Every time a human or agent retunes the asserted color for a legitimate visual reason (WCAG contrast fix, palette rebalancing), the test breaks even though no regression occurred, forcing a follow-up PR whose only purpose is updating the literal to match the new value. In this repo this happened twice in a 2-week window: PR #15525 tuned dark-mode colors in docs/components/DispatchIllustration.astro and TerminalDemo.astro, which broke two literal-color assertions in tests/unit/docs-accessibility.test.mjs and tests/unit/landing-page-diagram.test.mjs, requiring the separate follow-up PR #15538 to update the regexes to the new literals; then PR #15544 (another contrast retune of the same files, same self-care:accessibility-checker workflow) changed --terminal-syntax-placeholder from #ffbe88 and did not update the still-brittle assertion in tests/unit/landing-page-diagram.test.mjs, so at HEAD (commit 2fefc8f0) `node --test tests/unit/landing-page-diagram.test.mjs` fails: `assert.match(terminal, /--terminal-syntax-placeholder: #ffa657/)` no longer matches the current `#ffbe88` value — a real, currently-failing regression the rule would have caught before merge.
payload.mechanical_correction: Replace the literal hex/color-mix value assertion with a structural assertion: assert the CSS custom property or selector is defined with some color value (e.g. /--terminal-syntax-placeholder: #[0-9a-fA-F]{3,8}/ or a capture-group-based contrast check), or compute/assert contrast ratio programmatically (e.g. via a WCAG contrast helper) rather than string-matching the designer's exact chosen value. Where the test's actual intent is 'this token still meets AA contrast', assert that computed property, not the literal.

evidence.detail: Retuned many color-mix()/hex literals across docs/components/DispatchIllustration.astro and docs/components/TerminalDemo.astro for a real WCAG 2.2 AA contrast fix (axe-core violations), including --terminal-syntax-placeholder: #ffd1a1 -> #ffa657.

evidence.title: Align documentation contrast assertions with the updated palette

evidence.title: Improve dark theme contrast in docs hero illustrations
evidence.detail: A second contrast retune of the same two files (--terminal-syntax-placeholder: #ffa657 -> #ffbe88 and multiple color-mix literals in DispatchIllustration.astro) merged without a corresponding test update, leaving tests/unit/landing-page-diagram.test.mjs's literal-color assertion failing at HEAD; confirmed by running `node --test tests/unit/landing-page-diagram.test.mjs` locally against commit 2fefc8f0 (1 failing test, ERR_ASSERTION on the --terminal-syntax-placeholder literal).

payload.likely_false_positives: Asserting a literal color value is legitimate when the test is specifically about a fixed brand constant that is never expected to change (e.g. a GitHub/Primer base token that is not part of an actively-tuned theme), or when the assertion is paired with a computed contrast-ratio check rather than being the sole guard. The rule should flag literal hex/color-mix matches against files under active visual-design iteration (docs/components/*.astro, src/styles.js) rather than every color literal in the codebase.
payload.existing_plugin_coverage: No published ESLint rule covers this: it requires recognizing brittle golden-value regex assertions tied to a specific pair of source/test files under active design churn, not a generic no-magic-numbers or regex-literal rule that existing plugins (eslint-plugin-jest, eslint-plugin-regexp) target.
